liver ischemia-re-perfusion (IR) impairs aortal response to vaso-active drugs and that this dysfunction can be reversed by the antioxidant methylene blue (in a dose-response manner).

the effect of MB on the aortal dysfunction caused by liver IR in an isolated-perfusate ex vivo model.
an ex vivo isolated-perfused rat liver-aortal double-organ model to study the effects of hepatic ischemia-reperfuision on aortal function.
the effects of liver ischemia-re-perfusion injury (IR) on the aortal vascular bed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

MB, a potent antioxidant, is able to abolish the deleterious effects of IR liver effluent on the aorta, probably through the neutralization of reactive oxygen species and/or the restoration of the NO bioavailability.
MB is an effective agent in the treatment of IR-induced remote organ dysfunction.
MB, in a dose-dependent manner, reverses the deleterious effects of liver ischemia-reprfusion on the aortal tone and response to vasoconstrictor and vasodilator agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MB, at a concentration of 1.28mM, reverses aortic dysfunction induced by hepatic ischemia reperfusion.
MB is an effective agent for preventing aortal dysfunction in the setting of liver IR.
MB, a nitric oxide synthase inhibitor, can reverse aortal dysfunction induced by liver IR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MB may be useful in preventing aortic tone impairment induced by post-hepatic IR in a dose-dependent manner.
MB can be considered as a potential therapy for aortal dysfunction following liver IR.
IR-induced aortal tone impairment can be reversed by MB, and the best dose of MB is 1.28 mmol/L.
